notes: Topline: Argentum runs telemetry from 12k devices, spikes for firmware rollouts and incident windows; primary ask = deterministic inference for alert routing + embeddings search.
Deployment constraints: must live in customer VPC for ingest pipeline; on-prem appliance for air-gapped sites later phase. KMS integration required for keys.

Throughput/latency targets: critical-alert route => target p95 <= 120ms for short-context scoring (<=512 tokens); embeddings search p95 <= 300ms; bulk reranking jobs can be backgrounded and accept higher latency.

Cost sensitivity: unit economics matter — prefer baseline reserved capacity with burstable lanes rather than large permanent overcommit. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization.
- Priority lanes: explicit lane for 'critical-alerts' with guaranteed concurrency and token quota; separate lane for 'ingest-enrichment' and 'analytics-batch'.
- Tenant isolation: want per-tenant resource reservations inside Dedicated (soft reservations + hard caps) to avoid noisy neighbors across tenants and business units.
- Per-route quotas: ability to set token/sec and concurrent-request quotas per route + dynamic weighting for mixed traffic during incidents.
- Noisy-neighbor controls: cgroup-like capping, per-GPU scheduling priorities, preemptible background FIFO for non-critical jobs, and circuit-breaker fallback to smaller model variants.
SLA negotiations: looking for 99.95% uptime on edge services and p95 latency SLOs on priority lanes; legal requests a clause for credits if latency p95 exceeded for two consecutive days.

Reserved GPU planning: our sizing estimate pitched 8 A100-class GPUs for baseline 1k sustained concurrent short-context scorings with 2x burst capacity; customer asked for 12 month commit vs quarterly trial pricing.

Customer quote (paraphrase): 'We need deterministic behavior during incident windows — if a firmware rollout creates a 10x spike, critical alerts must still meet their SLO. We will pay for predictability.'
Notes on integrations: require SSO/SAML + SCIM for team management; audit-logging to 90 days; support for regional residency (US-only for now).
Open questions: how Redwood enforces per-route hard caps when requests are queued across multiple model variants; fallbacks for capacity exhaustion; billing granularity during bursts.
